5.q: A client asks the adviser in which situation an adviser would clearly have apparent, or ostensible, authority to act on a firm's behalf so that the firm becomes bound to a third party. Which scenario most clearly gives such authority?
o: The firm represents the adviser as authorised and the client relies
The adviser privately believes they have authority though never appointed
The client assumes authority because the adviser sounds confident
The adviser exceeds written limits but hides this from the client
5.w: Apparent authority arises where the principal represents that the agent has authority and a third party reasonably relies on it.

n.1: An agent's own belief does not bind the principal.
n.2: A client's assumption without a representation is insufficient.
n.3: Hidden limits alone do not create apparent authority.

5.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
5.q: Erin is advising Paul, aged 39, who describes himself as an adventurous investor but also says he will need the money in about four years to fund a new business venture. Why must Erin assess his time horizon alongside his risk appetite?
o: Time horizon affects the risk level
Time horizon sets the adviser's charging model
Time horizon replaces the disclosure duty
5.w: Time horizon governs how much volatility a client can tolerate, so it must shape the risk level recommended.

n.1: charges are not set by it
n.2: disclosure still applies
n.3: performance cannot be guaranteed

5.q: Alongside firm-specific supervision, the FCA carries out thematic reviews. How does the FCA use thematic reviews within its supervisory approach?
o: To review only firms reporting poor results
To assess risks across a whole sector
To investigate only firms in insolvency
To review fiscal policy for HM Treasury
5.w: Thematic reviews assess practices and risks across a whole sector or product type rather than a single firm.

n.0: Poor performance alone does not trigger a thematic review.
n.2: Insolvency investigations are separate from thematic reviews.
n.3: Fiscal policy is the Treasury's role, not the FCA's.

5.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
5.q: An adviser holds a scheduled annual review with Hassan, aged 44, a salaried engineer who funds a regular savings plan directly from his monthly pay. Several recent events are noted in his file. Which of these would require an immediate review of Hassan's affordability?
o: Loss of a primary income source
5.w: Losing an income source directly affects affordability and capacity for loss, requiring immediate review to prevent detriment.

n.0: Corrections do not directly change affordability.
n.1: Dividend changes are not affordability triggers.
n.2: Fee adjustments are rarely urgent.

5.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
5.q: An adviser reviews the personal circumstances of Priya, aged 31, since her last meeting. Several events are noted in the fact-find update. Which of these would most likely prompt the adviser to review Priya's protection arrangements?
5.w: Major life events such as a new child create new responsibilities and require protection needs to be reviewed.

n.0: Bond yields rarely alter protection needs.
n.2: Dividends are routine, not a trigger.
n.3: Adviser employment does not change protection needs.

5.q: Harriet is drafting her will with her adviser, Paul, and includes a clause stating that any beneficiary must outlive her by 28 days, failing which their gift fails and passes elsewhere. Harriet asks Paul what this type of clause is called. Which rule is this?
5.w: A survivorship clause requires a beneficiary to survive the testator by a set period, commonly 28 days, or the gift lapses.

n.1: Intestacy applies only where there is no valid gift.
n.2: Per stirpes governs distribution among descendants.
n.3: Anti-lapse provisions apply to certain relatives, not survival periods.

5.q: Which regulator has a secondary competition objective that it must pursue when advancing its primary objectives?
5.w: The PRA has a secondary competition objective, facilitating effective competition when advancing safety and soundness.

n.1: The FCA has competition as a primary objective.
n.2: The FOS resolves complaints.
n.3: HM Treasury sets policy, not a statutory competition objective here.

5.q: Shortly after adviser Raj recommends a monthly savings plan to Tom, aged 34, Tom is unexpectedly made redundant and his income falls sharply. Why is flexibility an important skill when a client's circumstances change so suddenly?
o: It guarantees Tom a consistently positive financial outcome
It lets Raj adapt recommendations to new circumstances
It exempts Raj from keeping records
5.w: Flexibility lets advisers adjust plans quickly when clients face unforeseen changes such as illness, redundancy or inheritance.

n.0: outcomes cannot be guaranteed
n.2: disclosure duties still apply
n.3: records must still be maintained

5.q: A client posts a signed letter accepting an insurer's offer, but the letter is delayed in the post and arrives late. The adviser explains how the postal rule applies. Under the postal rule, when does the acceptance take effect?
o: Only once consideration has been provided
When the acceptance is properly posted
When the offeror actually reads the letter
When received by the offeror at their address
5.w: The postal rule provides that acceptance is effective when properly posted, even if it is delayed or lost, unless excluded.

n.0: Consideration is a separate requirement, not the trigger for acceptance.
n.2: Reading by the offeror is not required under the postal rule.
n.3: Receipt governs instantaneous communications, not posted acceptances.

5.q: Consumer protection must sit alongside the FCA's competition and integrity aims. Why is the FCA required to balance its consumer protection objective with its other objectives?
o: To centralise all authority under Treasury
To let the PRA supervise conduct
5.w: Balancing objectives keeps consumer protection from undermining competition or integrity, delivering proportionate regulation.

n.0: Zero losses is impossible.
n.1: Authority is divided, not centralised.
n.3: The PRA does not supervise conduct.

5.q: What is the role of HM Treasury in relation to the statutory objectives of the FCA and PRA?
o: It sets the regulators' legislative framework
5.w: HM Treasury sets the legislative and policy framework, giving regulators their objectives and ensuring accountability to Parliament.

n.0: Firm supervision is done by the FCA or PRA.
n.1: Disputes are handled by the FOS.
n.3: Interest rates are set by the MPC.

5.q: What is the Bank of England's resolution objective under the Banking Act 2009?
o: Guaranteeing the profitability of failing banks
5.w: The Bank's resolution objective is to protect and enhance financial stability while minimising public costs and maintaining critical services.

n.0: Resolution does not guarantee profitability.
n.2: Consumer protection is the FCA’s remit.
n.3: Borrowing is managed by HM Treasury and the DMO.

5.q: An authorised advice firm decides to outsource its client administration and valuation reporting to a specialist third-party provider to cut costs. The compliance officer reminds the directors of the regulatory position before the contract is signed. What obligation applies to the firm when it outsources client services to a third party?
o: The client must waive their rights
5.w: Firms may outsource functions but cannot outsource regulatory responsibility, which stays with the authorised firm.

n.0: Liability cannot be shifted to the outsourcer.
n.2: The FCA supervises the firm, not the outsourcer.
n.3: Client rights cannot be waived.

5.q: Hannah is preparing a suitability report for Robert, aged 60, following her recommendation to consolidate two workplace pensions worth around £150,000 ahead of his planned retirement at 65, which he will read at home before deciding. Why is clear written communication so important in this document?
o: So clients understand reports and disclosures
It exempts her from any ongoing monitoring duties
5.w: Clear writing in suitability reports and disclosures lets clients make informed decisions and meets regulatory requirements.

n.0: Reports complement, not replace, meetings.
n.2: Writing cannot guarantee outcomes.
n.3: Monitoring is still required.

5.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
5.q: A firm requires its advisers to keep a structured, planned schedule of client reviews rather than reviewing clients only on an ad hoc basis. What is the main reason an adviser should maintain such a structured schedule of client reviews?
o: To guarantee the client's investment outperformance
5.w: Structured reviews give documented evidence that suitability is maintained and client interests remain central under FCA standards.

n.0: Reviews cannot guarantee outperformance.
n.1: Disclosure remains required.
n.3: Consumer Duty compliance is mandatory.

5.q: Walter dies intestate having never married, with no children and no traceable surviving relatives of any degree. His adviser is explaining what will ultimately happen to his estate. What happens to their estate?
o: It is retained by the probate registry
It is shared among local charities
It is transferred to the Insolvency Service
5.w: If no entitled relatives survive, the estate passes to the Crown as bona vacantia.

n.0: The probate registry does not retain estates.
n.1: Charities benefit only if named in a will.
n.2: The Insolvency Service does not handle intestate estates.

5.q: The resolution regime aims to let a failing bank exit the market in an orderly way. Which PRA Fundamental Rule requires firms to prepare for resolution?
5.w: Fundamental Rule 8 requires PRA-regulated firms to prepare for resolution so that failure can occur in an orderly way.

n.1: Fundamental Rule 1 requires integrity.
n.2: Fundamental Rule 4 concerns adequate resources.
n.3: Fundamental Rule 6 concerns organisation and control.

5.q: A firm is explaining to its board which feature of the Certification Regime does most to protect clients directly, rather than serving mainly internal purposes. Which element of the regime most directly protects clients?
o: Reduced regulator supervision of the firm
5.w: Annual fitness and propriety checks keep certified individuals capable and honest, protecting clients.

n.0: Dividends are unrelated to client protection.
n.2: Supervision levels are unchanged.
n.3: Promotion is separate from certification.

5.q: The PRA relies on timely, accurate information from the firms it supervises. Which Fundamental Rule requires firms to maintain effective information systems for regulators?
5.w: PRA Fundamental Rule 7 requires firms to deal openly with regulators and provide information as reasonably required.

n.0: Fundamental Rule 1 covers integrity.
n.1: Fundamental Rule 4 covers resources.
n.3: Fundamental Rule 5 deals with risk systems.

5.q: The PRA's core mandate concerns the stability of the firms it authorises. What is the purpose of the PRA's safety and soundness objective?
o: To guarantee a profit on investments
To ensure firms don't threaten stability
To set interest rates for households
To provide insurance cover to depositors
5.w: The safety and soundness objective ensures PRA-authorised firms operate so as to reduce the risk of systemic disruption.

n.0: Profits cannot be guaranteed.
n.2: Interest rates are set by the MPC.
n.3: Deposit protection is provided via the FSCS.

6.q: A firm identifies a breach itself and reports it promptly, cooperating fully with the investigation. What is the FCA's typical approach in these circumstances?
o: They are automatically exempt from all enforcement
They are fined the maximum by default
6.w: Firms that self-report and cooperate may benefit from reduced sanctions, reflecting the FCA's emphasis on transparency.

n.0: Exemption is not guaranteed; sanctions may still apply.
n.2: The FCA applies proportionality, not identical outcomes.
n.3: Maximum fines are reserved for the worst, uncooperative cases.

6.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
6.q: Following a review with Colin, aged 57, a client nearing retirement, adviser Ian and the client agree to increase his pension contributions and rebalance the portfolio towards lower risk. Ian carefully records the changes they agreed. What is the main purpose of documenting these agreed changes?
o: To evidence ongoing suitability and compliance
To remove the adviser's disclosure obligations entirely
6.w: Recording agreed changes shows adjustments were made to maintain suitability, supporting compliance and transparency.

n.1: Documentation does not replace annual reviews.
n.2: Disclosure is still required.
n.3: Performance cannot be guaranteed.

6.q: Adviser Jonah is closing a client relationship and asks how long the firm must retain the customer due diligence and transaction records it gathered under the AML rules. What is the minimum retention period required?
6.w: Firms must keep customer due diligence and transaction records for at least five years after the relationship or transaction ends.

n.0: One year is insufficient.
n.1: Seven years applies in tax, not AML.
n.2: Ten years exceeds the AML minimum.

6.q: A wealth manager holds cash and securities on behalf of its retail clients. Under the FCA's Client Assets Sourcebook (CASS), the firm must ensure these are handled correctly. What obligation applies when a firm holds client assets under CASS?
6.w: CASS requires firms to segregate and protect client assets so they stay safe if the firm fails.

n.1: Using assets to fund operations breaches safeguarding.
n.2: Automatic proprietary investment misuses assets.
n.3: Client ownership must be preserved, not transferred.

6.q: An adviser is asked by a client which statute governs how a person's estate is distributed where they have died without leaving any valid will. Which statute sets out the intestacy rules in England and Wales?
o: The Inheritance (Provision for Family and Dependants) Act 1975
6.w: The Administration of Estates Act 1925 sets out the intestacy rules, determining how estates are distributed without a will.

n.0: The Trustee Act modernises trustee powers, not intestacy.
n.1: The Law of Property Act governs property rights.
n.2: The 1975 Act allows dependants to claim provision.

6.q: A client is drafting a will, and one of the two people he asks to witness his signature is also left a small legacy under the same will. He asks his adviser what effect this will have. Where a person who witnessed a will is also left a gift in it, what is the effect?
o: The entire will is rendered invalid
The gift to the witness fails but the will stands
The will must be re-executed with fresh witnesses
The witness automatically becomes an executor
6.w: Where a witness or their spouse is a beneficiary, the will remains valid but the specific gift to that witness fails.

n.0: The will is not invalidated entirely.
n.2: No re-execution is needed; the will stands.
n.3: Witnessing does not confer executorship.

6.q: Sofia is designing a financial promotion for a higher-risk investment aimed at retail investors. Her compliance team reminds her of a key obligation about how the promotion should present the product to consumers. What is that key obligation?
6.w: Promotions must present a balanced picture of risks and rewards so consumers are not misled.

n.0: Benefits-only messaging would mislead.
n.1: Costs must be disclosed, not excluded.
n.3: Technical-only language obscures clarity.

6.q: Elaine holds savings with an authorised UK bank and wants to know how much of her money would be protected if the bank failed. What is the current FSCS limit for protected deposits per person per authorised bank?
6.w: The FSCS protects deposits up to £85,000 per eligible person, per authorised bank or building society.

n.0: £50,000 was the former limit.
n.1: £100,000 is not the deposit limit.
n.2: £150,000 exceeds the limit.

6.q: Gareth, aged 52, runs a plumbing business as a sole trader and, after losing his main contract, can no longer pay business debts of around £60,000. He asks his adviser which insolvency process applies to him, given that in law he and his business are one and the same person. Which insolvency process applies to him, as it would to any individual?
6.w: Sole traders are individuals, so bankruptcy is the equivalent process, allowing debts to be written off and assets realised.

n.0: CVAs apply to companies, not sole traders.
n.1: Administration is a corporate process.
n.3: Liquidation applies to companies.

6.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
6.q: At a review with Simon, aged 53, the adviser and client discuss several options for his ISA and pension but ultimately agree that no changes to his portfolio are needed at this time. Even though nothing was altered, why should the adviser still record the discussion?
o: To exempt the adviser from Consumer Duty
6.w: Recording the discussion evidences that client needs were reviewed and considered, even where no change was made, supporting transparency.

n.0: Performance cannot be guaranteed.
n.1: Review obligations remain.
n.2: Consumer Duty always applies.

6.q: Which FCA Principle requires a firm to conduct its business with integrity, forming the foundation of the principles-based regime?
6.w: Principle 1 requires firms to conduct business with integrity, the foundation of the FCA's principles-based regime.

n.0: Principle 2 is about diligence.
n.2: Principle 4 covers financial resources.
n.3: Principle 6 covers treating customers fairly.

6.q: Chloe advises a broad range of clients, from first-time savers to experienced investors with sizeable portfolios, and is paid partly through product commission that varies between providers. How does she best demonstrate professionalism in her dealings with the clients who come to her?
o: By keeping integrity, objectivity and client focus
By maximising commission regardless of outcomes
By replacing disclosures with her opinions
6.w: Professionalism means prioritising client interests, acting with integrity and giving objective advice that complies with FCA standards.

n.1: Commission-driven advice breaches FCA principles.
n.2: Opinions cannot replace disclosure.
n.3: Recordkeeping remains required.

6.q: In an ethics workshop, candidates debate the drawbacks of a purely compliance-driven mindset within an advice firm. The tutor asks them to pin down the key limitation, distinguishing it from what an ethical approach built on fairness and client trust would add. What is a key limitation of compliance-driven behaviour?
o: It ensures higher standards than ethical codes
It always protects long-term client trust
6.w: Compliance-driven behaviour focuses on avoiding breaches and penalties, while ethics focuses on fairness and trust.

n.0: Ethical codes often exceed compliance, not the reverse.
n.1: Trust depends on ethics, not compliance alone.
n.3: Rules do not automatically produce ethical reasoning.

6.q: Adviser Meg has resolved an ethical dilemma affecting her client's recommendation and explains the decision to him in plain, jargon-free language. Her trainee asks why the plain-language explanation matters. Why is this important?
o: To shorten the written suitability report
To speed up client product sign-ups
6.w: Plain language keeps decisions transparent so clients understand and can consent.

n.0: Report length is irrelevant.
n.1: Efficiency is secondary.
n.2: Sign-up speed is not the point.

6.q: Preventing market abuse and financial crime supports confidence in the markets. Which statutory objective of the FCA is most directly linked to tackling financial crime?
6.w: The market integrity objective covers preventing market abuse and financial crime to maintain trust.

n.0: Consumer protection addresses fairness.
n.1: Competition relates to choice.
n.2: Prudential safety concerns firm soundness.

6.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
6.q: Mona is completing a suitability assessment for Aisha, aged 37, who mentions that environmental and social issues matter deeply to her when choosing where to invest. Under the FCA's sustainability rules, why must Mona consider Aisha's sustainability preferences?
o: ESG funds will always outperform others
ESG preferences replace the full fact-find
The client may prioritise ESG factors
6.w: Clients may value sustainability, so Mona must record and integrate ESG preferences into the suitability assessment.

n.0: not guaranteed by ESG
n.1: preferences complement fact-finding
n.2: suitability still applies

6.q: A company preparing to list its shares on the London market must publish an approved prospectus. Which UK regulator is responsible for approving prospectuses for securities listings?
6.w: The FCA approves prospectuses for securities listings, ensuring investor disclosure and market integrity.

n.0: The PRA supervises prudential risk.
n.1: The Bank does not oversee prospectus approval.
n.2: The CMA handles competition law.

6.q: At a small advisory firm, a newly appointed staff member asks what the Money Laundering Reporting Officer actually does when colleagues raise concerns about a client. Which of the following best describes the core role of the MLRO?
o: To approve every new client account
To prosecute offenders in the courts
6.w: The MLRO receives internal reports of suspicious activity, assesses them, and decides whether to file a SAR with the NCA.

n.1: Legislation is set by government.
n.2: Account approvals are not the MLRO's core role.
n.3: Prosecutions are conducted by the authorities.

6.q: Rachel, aged 35, is investing a lump sum toward her retirement and asks her adviser why he recommends spreading her money across different assets, sectors and regions rather than a single holding. Why is diversification important when investing for long-term goals?
o: It reduces risk by spreading exposure
It removes all regulatory reporting obligations
6.w: Diversification spreads investments across assets and regions to reduce volatility and the risk of loss.

n.1: Diversification lowers risk but guarantees nothing.
n.2: Tax obligations remain regardless of diversification.
n.3: Regulatory duties apply whatever the strategy.

6.q: Under the FCA's Principles for Businesses, which Principle requires a firm to arrange adequate protection for clients' assets when it is responsible for them?
6.w: Principle 10 requires firms to arrange adequate protection for clients' assets, ensuring safeguarding on insolvency.

n.0: Principle 4 relates to financial resources.
n.1: Principle 6 covers fair treatment.
n.2: Principle 7 concerns client communications.

6.q: Leah manages a busy caseload of clients, each with fact-finds, suitability reports, disclosure documents and review dates to track. How do strong organisational skills support her in delivering effective and compliant advice?
o: They keep documents, disclosures and data accurate
They exempt her from suitability reporting
6.w: Good organisation lets advisers manage information accurately and deliver timely advice, supporting regulatory compliance.

n.0: Organisation cannot guarantee returns.
n.1: Annual reviews are still needed.
n.3: Suitability reporting remains required.

6.q: The FCA and PRA publish their statutory objectives and how they pursue them. Why does FSMA require regulators to publish their statutory objectives?
o: To remove the need for scrutiny
6.w: Publishing objectives makes regulators transparent and accountable, subject to scrutiny in delivering their mandates.

n.1: Regulators are not profit-making bodies.
n.2: HM Treasury retains oversight.
n.3: Parliamentary scrutiny remains essential.

6.q: A firm introduces formal recognition for advisers who raise concerns about fairness, even where no breach of the rules is actually involved. The board asks why this scheme should be regarded as demonstrating ethics. Why does rewarding advisers for raising fairness concerns demonstrate ethics?
o: It rewards integrity beyond the rulebook
It reduces the number of compliance audits
It eliminates the need for staff training
6.w: Rewarding fairness encourages integrity in practice, embedding ethics deeper than compliance requirements.

n.0: Approvals depend on compliance, not staff rewards.
n.2: Audits remain necessary regardless of rewards.
n.3: Training needs are not replaced by incentives.

6.q: Which FCA sanction is designed primarily to damage a firm's reputation as a deterrent, rather than to impose a financial penalty?
6.w: Public censure publishes misconduct details, harming reputation to deter without a financial penalty.

n.0: Prohibition orders ban individuals from regulated activities.
n.1: Restitution orders require compensation, not reputational harm.
n.2: Warning notices signal proposed action, not sanctions.

6.q: Which PRA Fundamental Rule underpins a firm's obligation to organise and control its affairs responsibly, extending to dealing fairly with policyholders?
6.w: Fundamental Rule 6 requires firms to organise and control their affairs responsibly, which extends to dealing fairly with policyholders.

n.0: Fundamental Rule 1 requires integrity, not fair treatment directly.
n.1: Fundamental Rule 2 concerns diligence, not fairness.
n.3: Fundamental Rule 5 relates to risk systems, not fairness.

6.q: Which regulator investigates potential breaches of conduct rules using supervisory visits, regulatory returns and market data analysis?
6.w: The FCA undertakes supervisory visits, reviews returns and analyses market data to identify conduct breaches.

n.0: The PRA focuses on prudential risk, not conduct.
n.1: The CMA enforces competition law.
n.3: The SFO prosecutes serious fraud, not routine conduct.

6.q: Why are custodians important within financial services, given the large volumes of client securities that must be safeguarded and accurately settled?
6.w: Custodians safeguard and administer client securities, ensuring safekeeping and accurate settlement, which supports trust in markets.

n.0: Deposit insurance is provided by the FSCS, not custodians.
n.1: Accounting standards are issued by the IASB, not custodians.
n.3: Corporate tax is managed by HMRC, not custodians.

6.q: A firm is training every member of staff, from its receptionists to its advisers, on the first-tier Individual Conduct Rules that apply to them all. Which obligation applies to all staff under those first-tier Conduct Rules?
6.w: First-tier Conduct Rules apply to all staff and require acting with integrity, underpinning client trust.

n.0: Returns cannot be guaranteed.
n.2: Suppressing complaints breaches openness.
n.3: Profit cannot be placed above fairness.

6.q: An adviser sets out with his client Owen, who has both some spare cash and an expensive credit-card balance, which step should generally come before committing any money to long-term investments. Which priority is typically placed before long-term investing?
6.w: Clearing high-interest debt prevents borrowing costs eroding wealth, so it usually precedes discretionary investing.

n.0: Market exposure comes after stability is established.
n.1: Insurance and equities meet different needs.
n.2: FCA oversight is ongoing and unrelated.

6.q: To ensure a failing bank can be wound down without destabilising the wider system, which UK statutory framework requires banks to prepare recovery and resolution plans, often called 'living wills'?
6.w: The Banking Act 2009 introduced recovery and resolution planning, requiring banks to prepare 'living wills' for orderly wind-down.

n.0: The MiFID II Directive governs markets and investor protection, not wind-down.
n.2: The Solvency II Directive applies to insurers, not banks.
n.3: The UCITS Directive covers investment funds, not bank recovery.

6.q: Which FCA enforcement action can require a firm to cease carrying on certain regulated activities with immediate effect?
6.w: The FCA can vary or withdraw a firm's permission, requiring it to stop certain regulated activities immediately.

n.0: Public censure exposes misconduct but does not restrict permissions.
n.2: Final notices confirm completed action, not immediate restrictions.
n.3: Thematic reviews assess sector practice, not individual restrictions.

6.q: Many consumers struggle to understand products such as pensions and mortgages. What is the Government's role in relation to financial education?
6.w: The Government supports financial education through policy, curriculum design and campaigns to improve understanding of financial products.

n.0: Insurance is provided by firms and schemes, not the Government.
n.2: Global standards are coordinated by Basel, not the UK alone.
n.3: Advisers are regulated by the FCA, not the Government.

6.q: The FCA's work flows from a single overarching statutory aim. Under FSMA, what is the FCA's strategic objective?
6.w: FSMA sets the FCA's strategic objective as ensuring that relevant markets function well.

n.0: Profitability is not a statutory objective.
n.1: Protection is appropriate, not absolute, so zero detriment is not the aim.
n.2: Monetary policy is the Bank of England's remit.

6.q: Competitive markets give consumers genuine choice and fair pricing. Which FCA operational objective ensures consumers can access fair products and services?
6.w: The effective competition objective promotes competitive markets in the interests of consumers, ensuring fair choice and pricing.

n.0: Consumer protection focuses on safeguards.
n.1: Market integrity concerns confidence and stability.
n.2: Prudential supervision is a PRA function.

6.q: Karl works with clients from many different cultural and religious backgrounds, some of whom hold specific views on savings, borrowing, interest and how their money should be invested for their families. Why is cultural awareness an important skill for him?
o: It removes the need for any client disclosure
6.w: Cultural awareness helps advisers respect different perspectives and preferences, keeping advice sensitive, relevant and fair.

n.0: Approval is not guaranteed.
n.2: Disclosure remains required.
n.3: Suitability checks cannot be replaced.

6.q: After a serious personal-data breach at an advice firm, the compliance team needs to identify which UK body has the power to impose administrative fines for that breach. Which body is this?
6.w: The ICO can impose administrative fines for breaches of the Data Protection Act 2018 and UK GDPR.

n.0: The FCA does not enforce data protection.
n.1: The PRA regulates prudential matters.
n.2: The NCA handles financial crime intelligence.

6.q: Insider dealing can be prosecuted as a criminal offence in the UK. What is the maximum criminal sentence for insider dealing under the Criminal Justice Act 1993?
o: Two years and a capped fine
Only financial penalties, with no imprisonment
Seven years and/or an unlimited fine
6.w: The Criminal Justice Act 1993 sets a maximum of seven years' imprisonment and/or an unlimited fine for insider dealing.

n.0: The maximum is higher than two years.
n.1: A ban is regulatory, not the statutory criminal maximum.
n.2: Imprisonment is a core sanction under the Act.

6.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
6.q: One of the structured investment plans held by Malcolm, an existing client aged 60, has had its terms altered significantly by the provider, changing the way its returns are calculated. When his adviser becomes aware of this change, what is the adviser obliged to do?
o: Ignore the change until the client raises it
Assume the provider has explained it
Guarantee the change has no effect
Reassess suitability and inform the client
6.w: Significant product changes must be reviewed for suitability, and the client informed, to maintain transparency and compliance.

n.0: Ignoring it risks unsuitable advice.
n.1: Advisers cannot rely on providers to communicate.
n.2: Outcomes cannot be guaranteed.

6.q: The board of a mid-sized adviser network is reviewing its governance arrangements in light of the SM&CR, and the chair asks why leadership must establish clear accountability under the regime. Which explanation best reflects the purpose of establishing that accountability?
o: To avoid producing annual financial statements
To eliminate capital adequacy testing entirely
To prevent regulators from supervising the firm
To allocate clear responsibility for conduct
6.w: SM&CR requires clear allocation of accountability for conduct and culture to named individuals.

n.0: Financial statements remain required regardless.
n.1: Capital adequacy testing is a prudential duty, unaffected.
n.2: Regulator supervision continues under SM&CR.

6.q: Which body is responsible for administering and maintaining the UK Corporate Governance Code, which sets standards for board leadership and accountability?
6.w: The Financial Reporting Council maintains the UK Corporate Governance Code, setting standards for board leadership and accountability.

n.0: The FCA regulates conduct but does not maintain the Code.
n.2: The PRA oversees prudential risk, not governance codes.
n.3: The IASB sets accounting standards, not governance codes.

6.q: A client considering referring a complaint to the Financial Ombudsman Service asks his adviser how much the ombudsman can order a firm to pay. The complaint concerns advice given in 2021. What is the maximum monetary award the Financial Ombudsman Service can order for acts on or after 1 April 2019?
6.w: For acts or omissions on or after 1 April 2019, the maximum FOS award is £350,000 plus interest and costs.

n.0: £150,000 was the former limit.
n.2: £250,000 is not the current maximum.
n.3: £500,000 exceeds the award limit.

6.q: A client married for the first time last month, having made a will several years earlier that made no reference to any future marriage. She asks her adviser what effect the marriage has had on that existing will. What is the effect of the marriage on that will?
o: It automatically amends the will to include the new spouse
It revokes the will unless made in contemplation of it
It has no effect at all on the existing will
It revokes only the clauses relating to property
6.w: Under the Wills Act 1837, marriage revokes a will unless it was expressly made in contemplation of that marriage.

n.0: The law does not automatically amend wills.
n.2: Marriage does affect the will, subject to the exception.
n.3: The whole will is revoked, not only property clauses.

6.q: Once enforcement action is complete, the FCA places a lasting public record of it on the register. Which notice is that final public record of the action taken?
6.w: A final notice is published to record the FCA's enforcement decision once appeal processes are complete.

n.0: Decision notices precede final notices and may be appealed.
n.1: Warning notices are earlier in the process.
n.2: Injunctions stop behaviour but are not notices.

6.q: The PRA supervises insurers under a dedicated statutory aim. Which PRA objective specifically applies to the insurance sector?
6.w: The PRA's policyholder protection objective is to contribute to securing an appropriate degree of protection for policyholders.

n.1: Consumer protection is an FCA objective.
n.2: Market integrity is an FCA responsibility.
n.3: Competition is not insurance-specific.

6.q: Which FCA operational objective is most directly linked to ensuring consumers are treated fairly when purchasing financial products?
6.w: The consumer protection objective secures an appropriate degree of protection, including fair treatment in product sales.

n.0: Market integrity concerns trust in the system.
n.1: Competition focuses on market dynamics.
n.2: Prudential safety is the PRA's remit.

6.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
6.q: Priya keeps detailed notes of every phone call and meeting with her clients, including Martin, aged 59, recording what was discussed, the options considered and the decisions agreed. Why is maintaining such records essential to her regulated advice?
o: To evidence compliance and support fair outcomes
To take the place of preparing suitability reports
To remove the need for reviews
6.w: Detailed records evidence compliance with FCA rules and help demonstrate that advice delivered fair client outcomes.

n.1: Records supplement, not replace, suitability reports.
n.2: Reviews are still required.
n.3: Commission disclosure is only one part of record-keeping.

6.q: A married couple own their home as joint tenants. On advice, they decide to sever the joint tenancy so that each can leave their share of the property to someone else by will. What is the main legal effect of severing a joint tenancy?
o: It transfers the property to a third party
It voids the original purchase contract
It becomes a tenancy in common
6.w: Severance removes the right of survivorship, creating a tenancy in common so each party can leave their share by will.

n.0: Severance changes the form of co-ownership, not ending it.
n.1: Severance does not transfer to third parties.
n.2: The purchase contract stays valid.

6.q: The FCA seeks to keep the financial system transparent, orderly and able to withstand shocks. Which statutory objective underpins this duty?
6.w: The market integrity objective requires the FCA to protect and enhance confidence in the system, ensuring transparency and resilience.

n.0: Consumer protection safeguards individuals.
n.1: Competition promotes choice.
n.2: Prudential supervision is the PRA's remit.

6.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
6.q: Gary is recommending a stocks and shares ISA to Rita, aged 50, who wants medium-term growth with access to her money after around five years. Before finalising, Gary cross-checks her stated objectives against the product's features, risks and charges. Why must he do this?
o: To raise the sales conversion rate
To remove the need for annual reviews
To lift the firm's regulatory capital
6.w: Matching objectives to product features makes the advice suitable, documented and defensible.

n.0: not the reason for the requirement
n.1: reviews are still required
n.3: unrelated to suitability

6.q: The UK's financial regulators must answer to elected representatives for their performance. Which regulator is directly accountable to Parliament for its statutory objectives?
o: Both the FCA and the PRA
6.w: Both the FCA and PRA are independent regulators accountable to Parliament for achieving their statutory objectives.

n.0: The PRA is also accountable, not just the FCA.
n.1: The FCA is also accountable.
n.2: Accountability extends to the PRA and FCA separately.

6.q: A secured lender to an insolvent company holds both a fixed and a floating charge over its assets and wants to appoint someone to realise those charged assets and repay the debt owed to it. The adviser is asked which insolvency process permits this. Which process lets a secured creditor appoint a receiver to realise assets subject to a fixed or floating charge?
6.w: Receivership enables a secured creditor to appoint a receiver to realise charged assets and repay the debt owed to them.

n.0: Liquidation is not initiated directly by secured creditors.
n.1: A CVA is a compromise, not enforcement of security.
n.3: Administration aims to rescue the business, not enforce security.

6.q: Emma is advising Rachel, aged 39, who has recently been through a difficult divorce, is managing money on her own for the first time and feels anxious and upset about her finances. How does showing empathy help Emma in her interactions with this client?
o: It builds trust and stronger relationships
It exempts her from all regulatory reporting duties
6.w: Empathy helps advisers understand the client's perspective, building the trust and rapport essential to effective advice.

n.0: Suitability assessments are still required.
n.1: Empathy cannot guarantee results.
n.3: Reporting obligations remain.

6.q: An adviser needs to check the FCA's detailed conduct rules on suitability and disclosure for investment business. Which FCA sourcebook contains these rules?
6.w: The Conduct of Business Sourcebook (COBS) sets out FCA rules governing investment business, including suitability and disclosure.

n.0: CASS covers client assets, not investment conduct.
n.1: DISP covers complaints, not investment conduct.
n.3: SYSC sets governance standards, not detailed conduct rules.

6.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
6.q: During a fact-find, Beth's client Malcolm, aged 48, struggles to articulate what he wants from investing, saying only that he would like his money to grow and be there if he needs it. To reach suitable recommendations, what should Beth do?
o: Rely only on his past product choices
6.w: Structured questioning helps the client clarify objectives, which Beth must document to keep recommendations suitable.

n.1: bypasses suitability when objectives are unclear
n.2: may not fit the client's needs
n.3: do not establish current suitability

6.q: Before Marcus signs up to a new personal pension, his adviser provides a full breakdown of the charges he will pay. Compliance stresses that this pre-sale disclosure serves a clear regulatory purpose. Why must firms provide clients with cost transparency before a contract is concluded?
o: So firms can avoid FCA reporting
6.w: Pre-sale cost disclosure lets clients compare products and assess suitability, supporting transparency and fairness.

n.0: FCA reporting obligations remain regardless.
n.2: Commission focus is not a regulatory purpose.
n.3: Cooling-off rights are not affected by disclosure.

6.q: Adviser Priya is about to arrange a personal pension for a retail client and needs to hand over the key information on the plan's features, risks and costs. She wants to be sure she does so at the correct point in the process. When must a firm provide such key information to a retail client before a contract?
o: Only at the annual review meeting
6.w: Pre-contract disclosures must be given in good time so clients can assess suitability and costs before committing.

n.0: Post-sale disclosure is too late to inform the decision.
n.2: Annual reviews occur after the sale, not before.
n.3: Firms must disclose proactively, not only on request.

6.q: Elena, a widow with three adult children whose financial circumstances and reliability differ considerably, wants her trustees to decide how much each child receives and when, rather than fixing their entitlements now. Her adviser is recommending a suitable structure. Which trust best achieves her aim?
o: A trust giving each beneficiary a fixed income
A trust that must distribute all income equally
A trust where the settlor keeps full control
6.w: In a discretionary trust, the trustees decide how and when beneficiaries receive benefits, giving flexibility in estate planning.

n.0: Fixed entitlements describe a fixed-interest trust.
n.1: Discretionary trusts allow selective distribution, not mandatory equal shares.
n.3: The settlor gives up control to the trustees.

6.q: A client who is worried about the safety of the money she has invested through an authorised firm asks her adviser which body would compensate her if that firm were to collapse. Which scheme protects eligible claimants if an authorised investment firm fails?
6.w: The FSCS compensates eligible claimants when an authorised firm, including an investment firm, fails.

n.1: The FOS resolves complaints, not firm-failure compensation.
n.2: The PRA supervises prudential matters.
n.3: The Pension Protection Fund covers pension schemes.

6.q: The directors of Ravenscroft Capital adjust valuation data so the firm's accounts show a stronger solvency position than truly exists, hoping to reassure investors. An auditor later uncovers the manipulation. Which Principle 1 obligation is breached?
6.w: Principle 1 requires integrity; manipulating valuation data undermines honesty and fairness in conduct.

n.1: prudence concerns adequate resources, not honesty
n.2: this covers systems, whereas falsification breaches integrity
n.3: conflicts management is separate from misreporting

6.q: A firm's own dealing desk and its advisory arm may have competing interests. Which FCA Principle requires the firm to manage conflicts of interest fairly?
6.w: Principle 8 requires firms to manage conflicts of interest fairly, both between the firm and its clients and between one client and another.

n.1: Principle 2 concerns skill and diligence, not conflicts.
n.2: Principle 3 covers organisation and control, not conflicts.
n.3: Principle 7 covers client communications, not conflicts.

6.q: A firm's product review identifies that a feature of one of its investment bonds is likely to cause foreseeable harm to a group of its customers. Under the Consumer Duty, the firm must respond appropriately. Which action does the Duty require when such a feature is identified?
6.w: Consumer Duty requires proactive action to prevent foreseeable harm, including modifying or withdrawing a product.

n.0: Promoting a harmful feature conflicts with the Duty.
n.2: Hiding risks breaches transparency.
n.3: Firms must act before enforcement, not wait.

6.q: When the Financial Services Act 2012 restructured UK regulation, the FCA and the PRA were established as separate regulators. Why was the FCA created as a body distinct from the PRA?
o: To replace HM Treasury's fiscal role
To separate conduct from prudential regulation
To duplicate the Bank of England's core functions
6.w: The FCA focuses on conduct regulation while the PRA concentrates on prudential supervision, giving clearer accountability.

n.0: Fiscal policy stays with HM Treasury.
n.2: The FCA complements, not duplicates, the Bank.
n.3: Monetary policy remains the MPC's.

6.q: George, aged 50, is reviewing his various pensions with his adviser and wants to be clear about the single core financial need that retirement planning is designed to meet for him. Which financial need is most closely associated with retirement planning?
o: Paying down all debt at once
6.w: Retirement planning focuses on securing sufficient income for later life, often through pensions and investments.

n.0: Short-term speculation does not address retirement security.
n.1: Debt repayment helps but is not the core retirement need.
n.3: Discretionary loans are no substitute for retirement provision.

6.q: A product manufacturer is designing a new investment bond and must specify the type of client for whom it is appropriate, and those for whom it is not, under the FCA's product governance rules. Why must manufacturers define target markets under product governance?
o: To ensure good outcomes and avoid harm
To simplify the periodic disclosures given to clients
6.w: Target market definition supports Consumer Duty and PROD by aligning products to needs and preventing foreseeable harm.

n.0: Maximising commission is not the objective.
n.2: Product governance does not bypass suitability.
n.3: Disclosure simplification is not the purpose.

6.q: A firm is found to have given unsuitable advice to a number of retail clients. Which FCA Principle for Businesses is most directly relevant to this failing?
6.w: Principle 9 requires firms to take reasonable care to ensure the suitability of advice and discretionary decisions.

n.0: Principle 3 concerns organisation and control, not suitability.
n.2: Principle 5 covers market conduct, not suitability.
n.3: Principle 11 concerns regulators, not advice suitability.

6.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
6.q: Holly is considering a capital-at-risk structured product for Gareth, aged 52, a cautious first-time investor, but its target-market definition specifies experienced investors comfortable with losing capital, which does not describe him. What must Holly do?
o: Proceed if the client insists, unrecorded
Reclassify the client to fit the market
6.w: If the client falls outside the target market, Holly should not recommend the product and should look at alternatives.

n.0: exposes regulatory risk and client harm
n.1: not permitted to fit a product
n.2: PROD definitions are mandatory

6.q: What is the purpose of a restitution order made under the FCA's enforcement powers?
o: To compensate customers for losses from misconduct
To publicise a firm's misconduct openly
To bar an individual from all regulated activities
6.w: Restitution orders require firms to compensate affected clients for financial losses caused by misconduct.

n.1: Publicising breaches is done via censure or final notices.
n.2: Barring individuals is a prohibition order.
n.3: Suspension is a separate regulatory sanction.

6.q: Which FCA operational objective is intended to ensure trust and resilience in financial markets?
6.w: The market integrity objective maintains trust, resilience and transparency in financial markets.

n.0: Consumer protection concerns individual safeguards.
n.2: Competition fosters choice.
n.3: The secondary competition objective belongs to the PRA.

6.q: A firm's money laundering reporting officer is training staff on the three recognised stages of laundering, describing one in which criminals move funds through numerous complex transactions to distance them from their source. Which stage of money laundering involves concealing the origin of funds by layering complex transactions?
6.w: Layering separates illicit funds from their origin through complex transactions that obscure the audit trail.

n.0: Placement is the initial introduction of funds.
n.1: Integration is the final stage.
n.2: Structuring is breaking up transactions.

6.q: Integrity underpins all of the PRA's expectations of a firm. Which PRA Fundamental Rule requires firms to conduct their business with integrity?
6.w: PRA Fundamental Rule 1 requires firms to conduct business with integrity, underpinning all other prudential obligations.

n.0: Fundamental Rule 3 requires acting prudently.
n.1: Fundamental Rule 5 requires effective risk strategies.
n.3: Fundamental Rule 6 relates to organisation and control.

6.q: The PRA's Fundamental Rules underpin its prudential supervision. Which Fundamental Rule requires a firm to act in a prudent manner?
6.w: PRA Fundamental Rule 3 requires firms to act in a prudent manner, consistent with safety and soundness.

n.1: Fundamental Rule 1 covers integrity.
n.2: Fundamental Rule 2 covers diligence.
n.3: Fundamental Rule 5 relates to risk systems.

6.q: A firm is rolling out Conduct Rule training that is tailored specifically for its senior managers, going beyond the training given to other staff. The learning-and-development lead is asked to explain its purpose. What is the purpose of this tailored Conduct Rule training?
o: To exempt them from annual fitness assessments
To ensure they grasp their heightened accountability
To allow delegation of all oversight duties
To guarantee client portfolios always perform well
6.w: Tailored training ensures senior managers understand the enhanced accountability their roles carry.

n.0: Fitness assessments remain mandatory.
n.2: Oversight duties cannot be delegated away.
n.3: Performance cannot be guaranteed.

6.q: Adviser Nadia is preparing to advise a client on transferring a valuable defined benefit pension, a notoriously complex area. Her supervisor reminds her which Principle governs the standard of work required. Why does Principle 2 apply when a firm provides complex pension transfer advice?
o: It requires maximising the firm's profits
It requires due skill, care and diligence
It guarantees the client capital growth
6.w: Advising on pension transfers demands high expertise, so Principle 2 requires firms to act with due skill, care and diligence.

n.0: profit maximisation is not the purpose
n.1: execution-only bypasses advice; transfers need diligence
n.3: capital growth cannot be guaranteed

6.q: Which FCA Principle requires a firm to organise and control its affairs responsibly and effectively, with adequate risk management systems?
6.w: Principle 3 requires firms to organise and control their affairs responsibly and effectively, with adequate risk management systems.

n.1: Principle 1 covers integrity, not systems and controls.
n.2: Principle 2 relates to diligence, not organisation.
n.3: Principle 10 deals with client asset protection, not organisation.

6.q: Devlin Wealth is designing a new stocks and shares ISA aimed at first-time investors aged 25 to 35 with modest sums to invest. Its product governance team is deciding which Consumer Duty outcome obliges the firm to design and distribute the product so that it meets the needs of that identified target market. Which outcome applies?
6.w: The products and services outcome requires firms to design and distribute products for an identified target market.

n.0: Price and value concerns fairness of charges.
n.1: Support covers service quality, not design.
n.2: Understanding relates to communications clarity.

6.q: The FCA has investigated a suspected case of insider dealing and gathered evidence. Which authority is primarily responsible for bringing the criminal prosecution?
6.w: The FCA investigates insider dealing, but prosecutions are usually brought by the Crown Prosecution Service under the CJA 1993.

n.0: The FCA refers serious criminal cases rather than prosecuting.
n.1: The PRA handles prudential regulation, not prosecutions.
n.3: The Bank of England manages monetary policy, not prosecutions.

6.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
6.q: An adviser is prioritising which developments in a client's life warrant the fastest response. For Gemma, aged 40, a salaried professional who funds her whole plan from her monthly wages, which of these should prompt the most urgent review of her financial plan?
o: A slight change in fund performance
A change in the adviser's remuneration
6.w: A major life event such as job loss materially affects affordability, objectives and capacity for loss, requiring urgent review.

n.0: Short-term fund performance alone does not justify urgent review.
n.1: Adviser pay changes do not trigger client reviews.
n.2: Minor market moves are managed through strategy.

6.q: To maintain confidence in the audited accounts of major companies, which UK regulator is responsible for monitoring the auditors of listed companies?
6.w: The FRC oversees the regulation and monitoring of auditors to maintain standards in listed company audits.

n.0: The Financial Conduct Authority enforces market conduct, not audit oversight.
n.2: The Prudential Regulation Authority supervises prudential soundness, not auditors.
n.3: The Competition and Markets Authority enforces competition law, not audit monitoring.

6.q: A firm that receives and holds money on behalf of its retail clients must make sure those funds are protected and identifiable if the firm itself were to fail or become insolvent. Where should client money be held to protect consumers?
6.w: CASS requires client money to be segregated in designated accounts so it is protected if the firm fails.

n.0: A trading account commingles funds, breaching segregation.
n.1: A personal trust lacks the prescribed CASS protections.
n.3: A suspense account is a temporary holding, not the safeguarded location.

6.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
6.q: Theo, aged 38, set up a £250 monthly investment plan two years ago, but has now missed three consecutive payments. His adviser notices the pattern while preparing for a review. Acting in Theo's best interests, what should the adviser do?
o: Guarantee that the missed payments will soon resume
6.w: Missed contributions may signal affordability problems, so the adviser should reassess and adjust recommendations for sustainability.

n.1: Ignoring it risks detriment.
n.2: Future payments cannot be guaranteed.
n.3: Higher risk does not solve affordability.

6.q: An individual is found to have dealt in shares while holding inside information ahead of a takeover announcement. What type of sanctions can the UK authorities apply for insider dealing?
6.w: Insider dealing attracts civil sanctions under FCA rules and criminal sanctions under the Criminal Justice Act 1993.

n.1: Warnings alone would not deter insider dealing.
n.2: Training is not a sanction for insider dealing.
n.3: Restitution is not the primary sanction.

6.q: Law firms handling client money are subject to anti-money laundering supervision. Which body is responsible for anti-money laundering supervision of solicitors in England and Wales?
6.w: The Solicitors Regulation Authority supervises anti-money laundering compliance for law firms under the Money Laundering Regulations.

n.0: The FCA supervises financial firms, not solicitors.
n.2: The PRA oversees prudential soundness of banks and insurers.
n.3: The CMA oversees competition policy.

6.q: Which EU directive specifically regulates electronic money institutions, covering the issuance of e-money and the safeguarding of customers' funds?
6.w: The Electronic Money Directive regulates e-money institutions, covering issuance, safeguarding of funds and capital requirements.

n.0: The Solvency II Directive covers insurers, not e-money firms.
n.2: The UCITS Directive applies to investment funds, not e-money.
n.3: The Bank Recovery and Resolution Directive applies to bank resolution, not e-money.

6.q: A client who has been made bankrupt, with no aggravating features or allegations of misconduct in his case, asks his adviser how long it will be before he is automatically discharged. What is the typical automatic discharge period for a straightforward bankruptcy in England and Wales?
6.w: Most bankrupts are automatically discharged after 12 months, although restrictions may continue longer in serious cases.

n.0: 6 months is shorter than the statutory period.
n.2: 24 months is longer than the usual period.
n.3: 36 months relates to certain repayment plans, not discharge.

6.q: Adviser Grace conducts annual suitability reviews for clients whose portfolios are managed on a discretionary basis. Her compliance officer explains how Principle 9 shapes this ongoing service. How does Principle 9 apply when an adviser provides ongoing suitability reviews for discretionary portfolio clients?
o: By maintaining customer relationships of trust
6.w: Principle 9 requires firms to take reasonable care to ensure suitability, maintaining customer relationships of trust.

n.0: capital rules are unrelated to suitability reviews
n.1: execution-only does not involve suitability reviews
n.2: firms cannot guarantee returns

6.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
6.q: Midway through advising Elaine, aged 62, on consolidating her pensions, Dan senses she is unhappy about the pace and cost of the process and she voices her dissatisfaction. Before the advice report is issued, what should Dan do first?
o: Refer it straight to the Financial Ombudsman
Acknowledge it and resolve it promptly
Wait until the advice report has been issued
6.w: Promptly acknowledging and seeking to resolve the concern reflects DISP and client-centric conduct.

n.0: premature before internal handling
n.2: ignoring it breaches complaint rules
n.3: harms the client relationship

6.q: The FCA scrutinises attempts to manipulate benchmarks such as LIBOR. Which of its operational objectives most directly underpins this work?
6.w: Benchmark manipulation undermines market confidence, placing it under the FCA's market integrity objective.

n.1: Consumer protection is less directly linked.
n.2: Competition concerns market dynamics.
n.3: Prudential safety is a PRA remit.

6.q: Adviser Ian is writing up how he resolved an ethical dilemma over whether to follow a client's instruction that appeared to be against the client's own interests. He must decide what to capture on the file. Which factor should he document?
o: The options considered and the reasons
The firm's quarterly profit targets set
6.w: Recording the options considered and the rationale supports transparency and accountability.

n.1: Profit targets are commercial.
n.2: Sales achievements are irrelevant.
n.3: Holiday preferences have no bearing.

6.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
6.q: Hana asks her client Rebecca, aged 41, to complete an attitude-to-risk questionnaire and keeps the completed form on file before recommending a balanced portfolio. Why is it important for Hana to document this questionnaire?
o: It exempts her from the Consumer Duty
It guarantees that the fund performs
6.w: The recorded questionnaire is key evidence that the recommendation matches the client's risk tolerance and capacity for loss.

n.0: Consumer Duty still applies
n.1: it complements, not replaces, fact-finding
n.3: cannot guarantee performance

6.q: A firm's Consumer Duty board pack, prepared by compliance lead Dana, tracks policy persistency rates, complaint volumes and root-cause analysis across the whole product range each quarter. Why should firms monitor outcomes using measures such as persistency, complaints and root-cause analysis?
6.w: Monitoring outcomes identifies emerging consumer harm so firms can act to improve products, communications and support.

n.0: KPIs are internal metrics, not the purpose of monitoring.
n.1: Adviser turnover is unrelated to outcome monitoring.
n.3: Cross-selling is commercial, not harm detection.

6.q: Under the Financial Services and Markets Act, when the FCA proposes significant changes to its Handbook, what general duty must it satisfy before those rules can take effect?
o: Seek HM Treasury approval before any consultation
Publish rules without consultation if pro-competitive
Refer the proposals to the PRC for prudential sign-off
Carry out cost-benefit analysis and consult
6.w: The FCA’s rule-making powers require a cost-benefit analysis and consultation before making significant rules, subject to limited exceptions.

n.0: Treasury approval is not a blanket prerequisite.
n.1: Competition benefits do not remove the consultation duty.
n.2: The PRC does not sign off FCA conduct rules.

6.q: What is the primary purpose of the UK Debt Management Office (DMO)?
6.w: The DMO manages the UK government's debt and cash needs, mainly by issuing gilts and Treasury bills.

n.1: solvency oversight is the PRA's role
n.2: monetary policy is the Bank's role
n.3: consumer protection is the FCA's role

6.q: A trainee adviser asks her supervisor which kinds of disputes the Financial Ombudsman Service is actually able to consider, having assumed it dealt with any commercial disagreement. Which of the following correctly describes the disputes the FOS can consider?
6.w: The FOS considers complaints from eligible complainants, usually consumers and small businesses, against authorised firms.

n.0: General commercial disputes fall outside its remit.
n.2: Shareholder disputes are corporate matters.
n.3: Employment disputes go to employment tribunals.

6.q: Sanjay, aged 35, holds £4,000 in a savings account earning modest interest while also owing £3,000 on a personal loan. He asks his adviser whether he should keep adding to his savings or clear the loan first. Which factor should most influence whether Sanjay prioritises saving or repaying his debt?
o: The firm's current internal sales targets
Interest rates on debt and savings
6.w: High-interest debt often costs more than savings earn, so relative rates drive whether to repay debt or save first.

n.0: Sales targets do not shape personal financial needs.
n.1: Competitor marketing is irrelevant to individual choices.
n.2: Equity index levels do not settle this decision.

6.q: An insolvent client wants temporary protection from creditors enforcing their debts while an Individual Voluntary Arrangement proposal is being prepared and put to them. The adviser is asked which order provides this protection. Which order provides it?
6.w: An interim order protects the debtor from creditor enforcement while an IVA proposal is being considered.

n.0: A charging order secures a debt against property.
n.2: An attachment of earnings deducts money from wages.
n.3: A possession order allows repossession, not protection.

6.q: Priya sits on the risk committee of an advice firm and is comparing how success is defined across its departments. Some teams embed fairness into board reviews and reward transparency, while one team measures its performance purely by whether the regulator has issued any fines. She must identify the outcome that signals compliance limitation. Which firm outcome signals compliance limitation?
o: Success is measured by the absence of fines only
Governance embeds fairness into board reviews
Advisers are rewarded for transparency with clients
6.w: Defining success by fines avoided reflects compliance limitation without ethical depth.

n.1: Fairness in reviews reflects ethical governance.
n.2: Ethical dilemmas in training demonstrate ethics.
n.3: Transparency rewards reflect ethical culture.

6.q: How does the UK Government principally influence financial stability through legislation, given the statutory basis on which the FCA and PRA operate?
o: By setting daily rates for banks
By passing Acts defining regulators' powers
6.w: FSMA 2000 and later reforms give regulators their statutory basis, underpinning oversight of financial stability.

n.0: Bank rates are set by banks, influenced by the Bank of England.
n.1: Equity is issued by companies, not by Government.
n.3: Accounting standards are developed by the IASB and FRC.

6.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
6.q: Tara is advising Gareth, aged 52, who wants to double his pension fund within eight years yet describes himself as a cautious investor uncomfortable with any capital loss. His stated attitude to risk clearly conflicts with his ambitious growth objective. What should Tara do?
o: Ignore the conflict and simply proceed
Move the client to an execution-only basis
Follow the stated risk profile alone
Reconcile them and document the reasoning
6.w: Tara must reconcile objectives and risk tolerance through discussion and documented reasoning to ensure suitability.

n.0: breaches suitability requirements
n.1: removes responsibility; not appropriate
n.2: objectives must also be weighed

6.q: How does UK Government policy most directly influence workplace pension provision and the way employers and individuals save towards their retirement?
o: By issuing gilts only to schemes
6.w: Reforms such as automatic enrolment and pension tax relief shape how employers and individuals save for retirement.

n.0: Pension investments are run by trustees and providers, not Government.
n.2: Returns depend on performance, not a Government guarantee.
n.3: Gilts are issued to all investors, not only to schemes.

6.q: An adviser firm receives a detailed information requirement from the FCA as part of a supervisory review, requesting policy data, client files and management information. The compliance director considers how to respond consistently with the Principles. How should the firm respond to satisfy Principle 11?
o: Await the outcome of an internal appeal process first
Provide prompt, complete and accurate information
Defer until the next RegData return
6.w: Principle 11 requires timely, accurate and complete disclosure in response to a regulator's information requests.

n.0: internal appeals do not excuse delay
n.2: summaries risk omitting required information
n.3: deferring to routine reporting delays cooperation

7.q: Which UK government department is primarily responsible for fiscal policy and the overall management of the economy, including taxation and public spending?
7.w: HM Treasury manages the government's finances, including taxation and spending, setting fiscal policy that shapes financial services.

n.0: The Bank of England controls monetary policy, not fiscal policy.
n.2: The FCA regulates conduct, not fiscal policy.
n.3: The CMA enforces competition law, not fiscal policy.

7.q: Which regulator's statutory objectives explicitly include contributing to the protection of policyholders?
7.w: The PRA has a specific insurance objective to contribute to policyholder protection alongside its prudential aims.

n.0: The FCA protects consumers broadly but has no statutory policyholder objective.
n.2: The CMA enforces competition law.
n.3: The PSR regulates payment systems.

7.q: The PRA's Fundamental Rules set out core standards for the firms it supervises. Which Fundamental Rule requires a firm to conduct its business with integrity?
7.w: Fundamental Rule 1 requires firms to conduct their business with integrity.

n.0: Fundamental Rule 2 requires diligence, not integrity.
n.2: Fundamental Rule 3 concerns prudence, not integrity.
n.3: Fundamental Rule 6 covers organisation and control, not integrity.

7.q: FSMA 2000 sets out the objectives of the regulators in clear statutory terms. Why does the Act require such clarity in those objectives?
o: To let regulators replace fiscal policy
To reduce the number of regulated firms
To let regulators set tax rates
7.w: Clarity in objectives makes regulators accountable to Parliament and transparent to the public.

n.0: Regulators do not replace fiscal policy.
n.1: Reducing firm numbers is not the purpose.
n.3: Taxation is outside regulators' remit.

7.q: A firm is redrafting its suitability letters and key features documents and wants to be sure the wording satisfies the FCA Principle focused specifically on customers' information needs. Which FCA Principle underpins the need for firms to consider customers' information needs?
7.w: Principle 7 requires firms to pay due regard to clients' information needs and communicate clearly and fairly.

n.0: Principle 3 addresses organisation and risk management.
n.1: Principle 6 concerns fair treatment broadly.
n.2: Principle 10 concerns client asset protection.

7.q: Maria, aged 58 and recently divorced, has two children from her first marriage and a partner to whom she is not married. She holds a personal pension, a rental flat and cash savings, but has never written a will. Her adviser, James, explains the primary financial need that making a will addresses. Which need is it?
7.w: A will ensures assets are distributed according to the deceased's intentions, protecting dependants and estate goals.

n.0: Wills do not determine investment returns.
n.2: Inheritance may still be subject to tax.
n.3: Liquidity needs are separate from estate planning.

7.q: In an AML refresher, adviser Tomas is asked which single piece of legislation criminalises laundering the proceeds of all crimes, not merely the most serious offences. Which Act is this?
7.w: The Proceeds of Crime Act 2002 criminalises laundering the proceeds of any crime, not just serious offences.

n.0: The MLR 2017 set compliance duties, not the offences.
n.1: The Terrorism Act targets terrorist financing.
n.2: The Bribery Act deals with bribery offences.

7.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
7.q: Client Hannah's household income has fallen sharply since her last review after her partner was made redundant, yet she is still paying substantial monthly contributions into her investment plan. Her adviser becomes aware of the change. What must her adviser do about her regular contributions?
o: Wait until the next annual meeting
7.w: When affordability falls, advisers must reassess and adjust contributions to avoid detriment and keep advice suitable.

n.0: Unaffordable contributions risk client harm.
n.1: Delay could breach suitability standards.
n.2: Higher risk worsens the position.

7.q: The FCA has decided that an individual should no longer be permitted to work in regulated roles. Which sanction allows the FCA to ban individuals from carrying out regulated activities?
7.w: A prohibition order prevents an unfit individual from carrying out regulated activities, permanently or temporarily.

n.0: Public censure is reputational, not a ban.
n.1: Restitution orders require compensation, not bans.
n.3: Advisory notices give guidance, not enforceable sanctions.

7.q: An adviser is explaining intestacy to a client whose son has already died but left children of his own. The client asks how the estate is divided where a deceased child's own children step in and take that child's share. How is such a distribution described?
7.w: Per stirpes distribution means the children of a deceased heir inherit their parent’s share, preserving family branches.

n.0: Per capita gives equal shares to living heirs.
n.1: Pari passu applies in insolvency.
n.2: Survivorship applies to jointly held property.

7.q: What is the FCA's statutory competition objective designed to achieve?
o: Ensure identical pricing across all firms
7.w: The competition objective promotes effective competition that benefits consumers through choice, innovation and fair pricing.

n.1: Identical pricing would stifle competition.
n.2: Market risk cannot be eliminated.
n.3: Profits are not guaranteed by regulation.

7.q: An external consultant is assessing whether a firm's culture is genuinely ethical or merely compliance-focused, and reviews four different aspects of how the firm operates and measures its own success. Which of these approaches most strongly suggests a culture limited to compliance rather than ethics?
o: Encouraging open discussion of client fairness
Measuring success only by fines avoided
Embedding ethical principles in staff training
7.w: Judging success purely on fines avoided is defensive compliance rather than ethical ambition.

n.0: Open fairness discussion evidences ethics beyond rules.
n.2: Principle-led training reflects an ethical culture.
n.3: Challenging conflicts supports ethical behaviour.

7.q: Georgia, aged 38, has recently been made bankrupt and asks her adviser which of her various debts will actually be written off when she is eventually discharged. Which of the following is discharged by bankruptcy?
7.w: Most unsecured debts, such as credit card balances, are discharged by bankruptcy, giving the individual a fresh start.

n.1: Student loans are excluded and remain payable.
n.2: Court fines survive bankruptcy.
n.3: Debts arising from fraud are excluded from discharge.

7.q: The directors of a struggling but potentially viable company want protection from creditor enforcement while they attempt to restructure and rescue the business. Their adviser explains a corporate insolvency procedure that could help. What is the main purpose of administration as a corporate insolvency procedure?
o: To protect the company from creditor action while restructuring
To repay shareholders ahead of creditors
7.w: Administration provides breathing space from creditor enforcement to attempt a rescue or restructuring of the company.

n.0: Dissolution is the outcome of liquidation.
n.2: Creditors, not shareholders, are prioritised.
n.3: Directors may be displaced, but not always permanently.

7.q: When a firm breaches the rules, the FCA has a range of tools available. Which of the following best describes the FCA's enforcement powers?
o: It can only issue guidance carrying no penalties
It can impose fines, censures and restrictions
It prosecutes every criminal offence itself
Its role is limited to mediating disputes
7.w: The FCA's enforcement powers include fines, public censures, banning individuals, and restricting firms' activities.

n.0: The FCA can penalise breaches, not merely guide.
n.2: It refers most serious criminal cases to other authorities.
n.3: Dispute mediation is the FOS's role, not enforcement.

7.q: One of the FCA's operational aims concerns the safeguarding of retail consumers. What does the FCA's consumer protection objective require it to secure?
o: The elimination of all consumer risk
An appropriate degree of consumer protection
Universal access to free financial advice
7.w: The consumer protection objective is to secure an appropriate degree of protection for consumers in regulated markets.

n.0: Regulation cannot eliminate all risk.
n.1: Schemes like the FSCS cover specific cases, not all losses.
n.3: Free advice is not a statutory requirement.

7.q: A prudential supervisor is reviewing whether a dual-regulated firm is running its business cautiously enough to remain safe and sound. Which of the PRA's Fundamental Rules most directly emphasises prudence in the conduct of a firm's business?
7.w: PRA Fundamental Rule 6 requires firms to conduct their business prudently.

n.0: Rule 1 covers integrity.
n.1: Rule 2 covers skill, care and diligence.
n.2: Rule 4 concerns financial resources.

7.q: Sam is explaining a recommendation to invest in a stocks and shares ISA to Ruth, aged 55, who has limited investment experience and needs to understand the plan before agreeing to it. Why is clarity in verbal communication essential in this conversation?
o: Clients must understand it to consent
It exempts him from Consumer Duty
7.w: Clients need clear verbal explanations to understand recommendations, ensuring informed consent and compliance with FCA rules.

n.0: Clarity does not affect performance.
n.2: Written disclosure remains mandatory.
n.3: Consumer Duty always applies.

7.q: The board of Ravenglass Custody is reviewing how its leaders can show genuine commitment to protecting client assets under Principle 10. How does leadership demonstrate commitment to Principle 10 in client asset protection?
o: By ensuring strong governance over custody
By delegating asset protection entirely to others
By suppressing reconciliation failures from the board
By prioritising firm liquidity over client funds
7.w: Principle 10 requires safeguarding client assets; leadership must ensure governance over segregation and reconciliation.

n.1: Delegation does not remove asset accountability.
n.2: Suppressing failures undermines protection.
n.3: Client funds cannot be subordinated to firm liquidity.

7.t: Regulatory Advice Framework for Fair Outcomes
7.q: Marcus, aged 42, tells his adviser that a recent inheritance means he no longer expects to need his invested money for at least twenty years. Given this longer horizon, what should the adviser reconsider about the recommendation?
o: His risk appetite and scope for growth
7.w: A longer horizon may allow greater risk and growth opportunities, so strategy should be reassessed while suitability is evidenced.

n.0: No strategy guarantees higher returns.
n.1: Disclosure cannot be removed.
n.3: Review frequency must still match needs.

7.q: A platform provider suffers a cyber-incident that exposes customers' personal data, and the board must decide how to engage with its regulator. Following such an incident, which FCA Principle requires the firm to deal openly and cooperatively with the FCA?
7.w: Principle 11 obliges firms to deal openly and cooperatively with regulators, including prompt, accurate notification after significant incidents.

n.1: communications concern client materials, not regulator cooperation
n.2: this covers systems and controls, not notification
n.3: this addresses fair treatment, not regulator engagement

7.q: Spouses Anna and Ben hold their family home together as joint tenants. Their adviser is explaining what will happen to the property when the first of them dies. Which feature applies on one spouse's death?
o: The survivor takes the whole by survivorship
The deceased's share passes under their will
Each owns a fixed share sold separately
The title converts to tenants in common
7.w: Joint tenancy carries the right of survivorship: the deceased's interest ends and the survivor takes the whole.

n.1: Under joint tenancy the interest passes by survivorship, not by will.
n.2: Fixed shares are a feature of tenants in common.
n.3: Conversion needs severance; it is not automatic on death.
